bullets.title: July PCE barely rounds to 0.2%; September rate hike off table, 10Y breaks support
bullets.body: Core PCE came in at 0.2455% MoM (just rounding to 0.2%), headline at 0.156% — both ~5bps above consensus but not alarming. Real personal spending was flat; income +0.43% MoM (beat). The soft-enough print removed September hike fears, and the 10Y broke its 4.67% TRADE signal per Hedgeye, with JPM noting CTAs accelerating buying as yields approach 4.60%.

bullets.title: S&P flat at 7,675; NVDA earnings dominate narrative, pricing in 0.25% extra SPX move
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures flat around 7,675–7,679 with VIX at 15.53. The market's primary focus is NVDA earnings (expected 4:20 PM ET) — SPX options are pricing in an extra 0.25% of movement for Thursday due to NVDA's ~7.3% index weight. Friday's Jackson Hole adds another 0.5% of priced-in SPX volatility. 0DTE straddle at $25/32bps suggests PCE itself was a non-event.

bullets.title: Oil drops 3%+ on Iran-Oman Hormuz talks; Hedgeye targets $79
bullets.body: Brent and WTI fell over 3% (WTI ~$80.66) as Iran and Oman discussed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and satellite data showed Gulf producers ramping output. Iran's IRGC complicates the picture by tying full reopening to end of war and US blockade lift, but the diplomatic progress is enough to break oil's key technical levels — Hedgeye flagged WTI broke both $84 trade and $83 trend supports, setting a new downside target of $79.09.

bullets.title: 2Q US corporate profits surged 22.8% YoY; GDP unrevised at +1.5%
bullets.body: 2Q GDP was unrevised at +1.5% q/q annualized, but real final sales to private domestic purchasers were revised higher to +4.2%. Before-tax corporate profit margins rose 1.0ppt to 17.4% — near historic highs — driven by lower labor costs. July durable goods orders improved 1.1% m/m with broad-based industrial capex gains, though tech capital goods orders slipped 1.1% m/m.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence divergence widening; student loan delinquencies hit 10.6%
bullets.body: The spread between Conference Board consumer expectations and present situation widened further in August, with the gap persistently negative. UMich sentiment (more rate/inflation-sensitive) diverging from Conference Board (labor-focused). Separately, 10.6% of student loan balances are now 90+ days delinquent — the highest since 2020 — signaling underlying consumer credit stress.

bullets.title: Investors rotating to cash-return certainty; AI/momentum factor underperforming despite strong 2Q beats
bullets.body: Cash Return is the top-performing S&P 500 factor YTD at +14.1%, displacing Price Momentum (now 4th). Semis, tech hardware, and industrials posted 96%, 93%, and 87% 2Q beat rates respectively but saw flat-to-negative post-earnings returns. H100 GPU rental rates are rolling over, and global memory names are being discounted for post-2028 supply concerns. EPS Momentum vs Price Momentum long is up +23.8% since June 21.

bullets.title: High yield at all-time highs; healthcare sector up 7.8% in August on short squeeze
bullets.body: HYG hit a record high — inconsistent with recession narratives per multiple strategists. The GS 'Most Short Healthcare' basket gained +5.2% in a single day and +13% over one month. Hedgeye rates XLV its highest-conviction US equity sector long and remains long Europe and Japan; Nasdaq showing lower highs and is not preferred.

bullets.title: Reuters poll raises S&P 500 year-end target to 7,900; Wall Street cites earnings, AI, geopolitical easing
bullets.body: Wall Street consensus (Reuters poll) lifted S&P 500 2026 year-end target to 7,900 from 7,620 in the May poll, with Dow forecast raised to 54,500 from 52,500. Drivers cited: strong corporate earnings, booming AI investment, and easing US-Iran tensions.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings: $92.2B revenue expected (+97% YoY); UBS sees $3-4B upside with $107-108B October guide
bullets.body: NVDA is expected to report ~$92.2B in revenue tonight at 4:20 PM ET. UBS anticipates another beat-and-raise with ~$3-4B July-quarter revenue upside and October-quarter guidance of ~$107-108B on stable Blackwell demand. Citi raises estimates ~$1B/$1.5B above Street for July/October quarters ($300 PT, 24x FY27). Oppenheimer calls NVDA 'AI's best house' with $1T+ cumulative GB200/VR200 revenue 2025-27.

bullets.title: NVDA's $200B off-balance-sheet AI credit exposure by 2028 flagged as emerging risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley and multiple strategists are focusing on NVDA's use of its balance sheet as a strategic AI financing tool — shifting capital access from shells to components like chips/servers. MS estimates NVDA could carry ~$200B in AI-related credit exposure by YE28. ~$92B of AI-related new corporate credit issuance globally since July reflects demand; over $20B in data center debt hit the market in July alone, pushing IG spreads wider.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC delivers 1.5-1.9x efficiency vs NVDA; SemiAnalysis sees AVGO, CLS as beneficiaries
bullets.body: OpenAI's custom Jalapeño ASIC reportedly delivers 1.5x-1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7x-3.6x lower inference latency than NVDA chips. SemiAnalysis sees risk to NVDA, AMD, and CBRS from inference chip competition, with AVGO, CLS, and Samsung as the primary beneficiaries of the shift to custom silicon.

bullets.title: AI networking becomes bottleneck post-compute; constructive for AVGO, MRVL, ANET, optical vendors
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side notes (Citi, JPM, MS) converge on networking as the next AI infrastructure bottleneck as compute constraints ease. Citi explicitly favors NVDA networking, AVGO, Marvell, Arista, and optical vendors as primary beneficiaries. CSP capex estimated at $950B in FY26, +94% YoY, with JPM seeing no fundamental weakness signals for semis in the next 6-12 months.

bullets.title: META settles child harm case for $18B (bullish vs feared $1.4T); stock +4.9% pre-market
bullets.body: Meta agreed to pay ~$18B to 29 state AGs over 10 years ($12.7B to states, ~$5.3B contingent on YouTube and TikTok compliance). META will accrue ~$10B legal expense in Q3 but Q3 guidance is otherwise unchanged. The settlement is widely viewed as favorable vs. the potential $1.4T trial loss scenario. Stock opened +4.9% to ~$597.90. New teen safety controls include 2-hour daily limits and Night Mode.

bullets.title: Memory pricing recovering: DDR5 spot up to $3,600; MS forecasts 18% DRAM undersupply in 2026
bullets.body: Citi Korea tech tour found 64GB DDR5 channel spot prices improved to $3,600 from $3,000, better than market expectations. Morgan Stanley forecasts ~18% global DRAM undersupply in 2026 and ~14% in 2027, expecting DRAM prices +20-30%+ in 3Q26. NAND pricing also solid for eSSD as suppliers shift production mix. Memory pricing expected to trend up from August onward.

bullets.title: MATCH Act could ban nearly all ASML China sales; potential 15% revenue headwind
bullets.body: The MATCH Act, moving through House and Senate, seeks to ban all immersion lithography equipment sales to China. Jefferies believes the Act will likely pass in broadly current form before reaching the President, despite market skepticism that Trump will reject it. If passed as written, a ~15% ASML revenue impact is likely and newsflow is expected to pressure ASML multiples near-term.

bullets.title: JPM: CSP capex hitting $950B in FY26 (+94% YoY); EM equities at decade-high inflows, below-average PE
bullets.body: JPM's global thematic update sees hyperscaler capex growth revised higher for the next 3 years, with Big 3 backlog growth outpacing capex. EM equities are outperforming US YTD by 800bps, with annual inflows at ~$70B (highest since 2022), and EM 12m forward PE at 10.2x (1 std dev below average). Dollar (DXY) below 100, USD/JPY below 160. Fed pricing ~27bps of hikes in FY26.

bullets.title: High-beta vs low-vol correlation hits record negative; factor divergence at extremes
bullets.body: The 45-day correlation between high-beta and low-volatility stocks reached its most negative level on record, signaling extreme market divergence and potential mean-reversion risk. This aligns with the broader factor rotation away from momentum toward cash return and earnings quality.

bullets.title: INTU guides FY27 growth to 9-10% vs 11% consensus; TurboTax at 2-3% signals business model reset
bullets.body: Intuit's FY27 guidance disappointed across the board — revenue +9-10% vs ~11% consensus, TurboTax +2-3% vs ~5%, GBSG ~12% vs 15-20% prior medium-term target. The company is pivoting from ARPC expansion to top-of-funnel customer acquisition with new low-cost tiers (QuickBooks Free, TurboTax free), resetting medium-term growth. Stock down ~10-11% pre-market; multiple analysts cut PTs while maintaining buy/overweight ratings.

bullets.title: Oil weakness + PCE dovish print drives 10Y below 4.67% support; ECB hike September expected
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged the 10Y broke immediate-term trade support at 4.67% on oil weakness, creating a dovish bias. UST 2yr also broke support at 4.24%/4.21%. Separately, one strategist notes the ECB is set to hike in September, with positioning remaining long euro vs. short dollar. German exporter sentiment hit a 4.5-year high and Merz projects 1%+ GDP growth in 2027.

bullets.title: PANW explored DDOG and OKTA acquisitions before pivoting to CyberArk/Chronosphere; DDOG +5%
bullets.body: The Information reported Palo Alto Networks explored acquiring Datadog and Okta as recently as last year before those discussions ended. DDOG shares moved +5% in early trading on the report. PANW reports FQ4 imminently with Piper Sandler and DA Davidson expecting modest beats, though analysts debate whether Mythos/AI monetization can support durable reacceleration.
